research_text:
# Research brief

## 1. API and finding

`java.security.DigestInputStream` wraps an input stream and updates an associated `MessageDigest` as data is read while digesting is enabled. The finding’s **observed call sequence** refers to calls associated with the governed stream, not to a digest value. On the supplied description, the detector did not accept that sequence under the rule; the message alone does not identify the missing or unexpected event. ([docs.oracle.com](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/21/docs/api/java.base/java/security/DigestInputStream.html))

A read event does not by itself establish that a byte was returned or that the stream was read to end-of-stream. The supplied information does not establish how the detector handles aliases, exceptions, implicit closes, subclasses, delegation, or interprocedural calls; those are unresolved review questions.

## 2. Documented usage and remediation

Oracle documents the following API behavior:

- Construct the wrapper with an `InputStream` and a `MessageDigest`. Digesting is **on by default**. `on(false)` stops updates, and `on(true)` enables them; both are documented API operations. ([docs.oracle.com](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/21/docs/api/java.base/java/security/DigestInputStream.html))
- After the relevant reads, call a `digest` method on the associated digest to complete the computation. `digest()` resets that digest afterward. For intermediate digests, Oracle describes retaining and cloning the digest where the implementation supports cloning. ([docs.oracle.com](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/21/docs/api/java.base/java/security/DigestInputStream.html))
- In the documented Java 21 implementation, skipped data is not included, while data read again after `reset()` updates the digest again. Thus, the bytes actually read while digesting is on matter to the result. ([docs.oracle.com](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/21/docs/api/java.base/java/security/DigestInputStream.html))
- The inherited stream contract permits an otherwise valid `read(byte[], offset, 0)`, which reads no bytes and returns zero. The CrySL rule separately requires `len > 0`; the two requirements should not be conflated. ([docs.oracle.com](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/21/docs/api/java.base/java/io/InputStream.html))

Oracle’s API documentation does **not** give a remediation for this detector finding or prescribe the CrySL sequence. It documents the above usage and behavior. Its `InputStream` documentation additionally recommends promptly closing the stream after an I/O error in the documented bulk-read methods, because the stream may be in an inconsistent state. ([docs.oracle.com](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/21/docs/api/java.base/java/io/InputStream.html))

## 3. Compatibility and migration

`DigestInputStream` is documented as available since Java **1.2**. Convenience methods have their own version requirements: for example, `readAllBytes()` and `transferTo()` are documented since Java **9**, while `readNBytes(int)` is documented since Java **11**. ([docs.oracle.com](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/21/docs/api/java.base/java/security/DigestInputStream.html))

The reviewed API documentation does not specify a persisted format, wire format, compatibility guarantee for a changed usage, or migration procedure for existing stored or transmitted digests. Changes to which bytes are included in the digest can change the result; compatibility with any particular format remains an open question outside these sources. ([docs.oracle.com](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/21/docs/api/java.base/java/security/DigestInputStream.html))

## 4. Matching rule in the supplied CrySL source

The supplied file’s relevant clauses are reproduced verbatim:

```text
SPEC java.security.DigestInputStream
```

```text
FORBIDDEN
	on(boolean) ;

EVENTS
	c1: DigestInputStream(stream, digest);
	Con := c1;

	r1: read();
	r2: read(data, offset, len);
	Read := r1 | r2;

	cl1: close();
	Close := cl1;

ORDER
	Con, Read+, Close
```

([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CROSSINGTUD/Crypto-API-Rules/refs/heads/master/JavaCryptographicArchitecture/src/DigestInputStream.crysl))

The file declares `stream` as `java.io.InputStream`, `digest` as `java.security.MessageDigest`, `data` as `byte[]`, and `offset` and `len` as `int`. Thus its event patterns specify the constructor’s two parameters, zero-argument `read()`, three-argument `read(byte[], int, int)`, and zero-argument `close()`. The separately forbidden pattern is `on(boolean)`. **The patterns are not unrestricted name-only matches:** the file scopes them to `java.security.DigestInputStream` and specifies parameter lists. It does not state that an unrelated receiver’s method merely sharing one of those names matches. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CROSSINGTUD/Crypto-API-Rules/refs/heads/master/JavaCryptographicArchitecture/src/DigestInputStream.crysl))

The order condition is construction, one or more named `Read` events, then `Close`. Separately, the file requires `length[data] >= offset + len`, `offset >= 0`, and `len > 0`; requires the `generatedMessageDigest[digest]` predicate; and ensures `digestedInputStream[stream, digest]`. It does not name `read(byte[])` or the convenience methods as events. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CROSSINGTUD/Crypto-API-Rules/refs/heads/master/JavaCryptographicArchitecture/src/DigestInputStream.crysl))

**Source limits:** The CrySL file does not specify the detector’s handling of subclasses, inherited methods, implicit closes, or delegation. The URL points to a mutable `master` branch; the supplied SHA-256 was not independently verified against the retrieved file.

### Direct sources

- CrySL rule: `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CROSSINGTUD/Crypto-API-Rules/refs/heads/master/JavaCryptographicArchitecture/src/DigestInputStream.crysl`
- Oracle `DigestInputStream`: `https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/21/docs/api/java.base/java/security/DigestInputStream.html`
- Oracle `MessageDigest`: `https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/21/docs/api/java.base/java/security/MessageDigest.html`
- Oracle `InputStream`: `https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/21/docs/api/java.base/java/io/InputStream.html`
